swap_risks: HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LMV358IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=RR vs TLV9062IDR: IN=RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.

CAUTION BANDWIDTH & PHASE MARGIN: GBWP differs by 10x (LMV358IDR: 1 MHz p.7 vs TLV9062IDR: 10 MHz p.13); higher-bandwidth replacements can oscillate with capacitive loads or stray feedback capacitance without an isolation resistor.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 6.5x (LMV358IDR: 1 V/µs p.7 vs TLV9062IDR: 6.5 V/µs p.13); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 30000x (LMV358IDR: 15000 pA p.7 vs TLV9062IDR: 0.5 pA p.13); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 5.1x (LMV358IDR: 105 µA/ch p.7 vs TLV9062IDR: 538 µA/ch p.14); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 32% higher on LMV358IDR (LMV358IDR: 207.9 °C/W p.6 vs TLV9062IDR: 157.6 °C/W p.11); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: LMV358IDR requires Vs,min >= 2.7 V (p.5) vs 1.8 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.
engineering_verdict: LMV358IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and TLV9062IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because rail-to-rail input/output swing differs; GBWP differs 10x; slew rate differs 6.5x. Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 1 MHz (p.7) vs 10 MHz (p.13), supply ceiling 5.5 V (p.5) vs 5.5 V (p.10), Vos 7 mV (p.7) vs 1.6 mV (p.13), Ib 30000x gap (15000 vs 0.5 pA), voltage noise 39 vs 16 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LMV358IDR "5.5 V Absolute Maximum Ceiling — Destructive If Swapped into LM358 High-Voltage Boards" (p.5) and TLV9062IDR "6.0 V Absolute Maximum Supply Limit — Destructive in 12 V / 24 V LM358 or TL072 SOIC-8 Sockets" (p.10). BOM decision: Choose LMV358IDR when ultra-low supply current (105 µA/ch) is prioritized; choose TLV9062IDR when closed-loop signal bandwidth requires 10 MHz GBWP or DC precision demands <= 1.6 mV max Vos. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.6) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
